The following is a '''list of all butterflies found in the [[Indochina|Indochinese]] biogeographic region''' ([[Geography of Thailand|Thailand]], [[Geography of Laos|Laos]] and [[Geography of Vietnam|Vietnam]], [[Geography of Cambodia|Cambodia]], [[Geography of Burma|Myanmar]] (formerly Burma; part of British India until 1937), [[Peninsular Malaysia]] and [[Singapore]] in the [[Indomalayan realm]]).

The climate of Indochina is [[Subtropics|subtropical]] in the north, tropical further south. Indochinese terrestrial ecoregions include the [[Northeast India–Myanmar pine forests]], [[Northern Triangle temperate forests]], [[Myanmar Coast mangroves]], [[Chin Hills–Arakan Yoma montane forests]], [[Mizoram–Manipur–Kachin rain forests]], [[Northern Indochina subtropical forests]], [[Irrawaddy dry forests]], [[Irrawaddy freshwater swamp forests]], [[Irrawaddy moist deciduous forests]], [[Cardamom Mountains rain forests]], [[Chao Phraya freshwater swamp forests]], [[Kayah–Karen montane rain forests]], [[Northern Indochina subtropical forests]], [[Northern Khorat Plateau moist deciduous forests]], [[Northern Thailand–Laos moist deciduous forests]], [[Peninsular Malaysian montane rain forests]], [[Peninsular Malaysian peat swamp forests]], and [[Tenasserim–South Thailand semi-evergreen rain forests]].

The butterfly fauna of Indochina includes Indo-Burmese genera with a species-richness (a count of species within the genus) generally distributed from [[Physical geography of Assam|Assam]] to [[Sundaland]] ([[Sunda Islands]]), genera with a strong centre of species-richness in [[Geography of China|western China]] and the eastern Himalaya, genera with their greatest species-richness in Sundaland west of the [[Wallace Line]] and species endemic to Indochina.
